speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any pain during urination or blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: That combination of pain relieved by voiding, frequency, and dyspareunia is highly suggestive of a bladder issue; do you notice any urgency or a burning sensation when you try to urinate, and have you experienced any visible blood in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine culture. REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None; Cystoscopy: Normal urethra and bladder mucosa.

speaker: Patient
text: ul intercourse. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your urgency; based on your symptoms of suprapubic pain relieved by voiding, frequency, and dyspareunia, the most likely diagnosis is Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome
